title: Surpassing Sycamore: Achieving Energetic Superiority Through System-Level Circuit Simulation
problem: Classical simulation of quantum circuits requires enormous computational resources. The challenge is demonstrating that optimized classical tensor network simulation can outperform quantum processors like Google's Sycamore in both execution time and energy consumption.
motivation: Validating the practical efficiency of classical simulation versus quantum processors is critical for understanding where classical systems remain competitive and guiding investments in quantum technology.
method: The system employs multi-level optimization (global, node, and device levels) across a massively parallel tensor network simulation framework. It distributes computation across 2304 GPUs achieving 561 PFLOPS peak performance, using post-processing techniques to compute XEB metrics for quantum circuit simulation.
key_novelty: Achieving superior energy efficiency and time-to-solution compared to quantum processors through system-level circuit simulation with coordinated optimization across hardware hierarchy and massive GPU parallelization.
contributions: Largescale tensor network system with multi-level optimization achieving scalability to 2304 GPUs and 561 PFLOPS
Classical quantum circuit simulation achieving 42x speedup (14.22 vs 600 seconds) over Google's Sycamore
18x energy efficiency improvement (2.39 vs 4.3 kWh) compared to quantum processor baseline
Open-source framework enabling reproducible quantum circuit simulation at scale

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 1.8x better (2.39 kWh vs 4.3 kWh); 0.29 kWh variant

limitations: Comparison methodology and practical relevance of classical simulation advantage not discussed.
primary_theme: Classical quantum circuit simulation with energy superiority
